findings.title: Blocking: every outbound credential resolution scans the retained identity table
findings.rationale: The newly introduced ChannelCredentialResolver.resolve loads providerIdentities through the reverse current_channel_id relation (api-app/src/domain/channels/channel-credential-resolver.ts:24-27) and selects the identity in memory at line36. That relation is not indexed: schema.prisma:252-270 and the foundation migration at lines100-115 define only the identity primary key, the provider/external_resource_id unique key and a bu_id index; the later admitted migrations add a cleanup_state/provider index, never current_channel_id. The parent channel primary-key lookup and the foreign-key declaration do not index this reverse lookup. Consequently the resolver's identity query must inspect the global provider_resource_identities table to find the attached row, including indefinitely retained tombstones from other BUs. This is on each BFF/public response send (conversations.service.ts:207) and each eligible Typebot execution (incoming.service.ts:81), also registration/verification, rather than only an administrative cleanup path. Returned cardinality near one does not bound scanned work. This is a concrete newly introduced O(all retained identities) database access on the message path and meets the dispatch's unbounded-scan blocker criterion; no production latency or saturation reproduction is claimed. D-07's durable ownership must remain intact and D-08 requires this shared resolver, but neither approves an unindexed reverse scan. The current EPS EXPLAIN tests only the attempt idempotency key (number-onboarding-pcv.e2e-spec.ts:30-34); its 25-row plan and GET timings cannot validate or exclude this different access path.
findings.suggested_action: Fix within the current contract before accepting the performance/EPS gate. Prefer resolving the channel's exact provider/externalResourceId through the existing composite unique key and checking currentChannelId, buId and managedLifecycle, avoiding the inverse collection entirely. Alternatively add a schema-backed, versioned migration index on current_channel_id and keep the same ownership/trust checks. Do not remove tombstones, add a cache or relax tenant/generation predicates. Preserve the caller and acceptance tests, and add discriminating query-plan/query-log evidence for the actual resolver path with a material population of unrelated retired identities so an attempt-only EXPLAIN cannot mask a regression. Repeat only the checks affected by the chosen correction; unchanged FRC/BCI/RLS observations remain usable subject to source freshness.

overall_assessment:
One new blocking performance finding: the shared outbound resolver has a global unindexed reverse-identity lookup (NUM-PERF-01). No additional concrete request amplification, provider page walking, fetch-all scheduler reconciliation or newly introduced exhaustion path was established. This is an independent read-only performance/PCV judgment of the frozen ST-CON-01 local delivery, not a production or final security/TQA verdict. Routing evidence declares formal-reviewer gpt-6.1-sol/max and GO. I directly read the present new/untracked implementation and relevant manifest-allowed consumers, controllers, schema/migrations, provider adapters, frontend operation owner/polling, PCV/browser harnesses, runner/runtime configuration and the governing TODO/module/pcv-1 references. I independently verified 266 manifest/index reference entries with zero hash mismatches, including all214 frozen public-source entries (213 present and the approved absent slug-only spec), indexed artifacts/canon and supplementary API build references. No private dotenv, operational Git blobs or .local-files payloads were read or hashed; no tests, builds, runtime/provider probes or mutations were run for this review.

Access-path and budget assessment: registration reads by attempt id plus tenant, idempotency replay by the composite unique key, channel slots by buId/type (maximum two channel types per BU), credentials by unique channelId, webhook resource mapping and message dedupe by composite unique keys are structurally bounded apart from NUM-PERF-01. Business-unit lists project local channels and make no provider calls. The existing user-grant/tenant BU collections and tenant-scoped Typebot trigger matching remain proportional to their authorized sets; the touched Typebot change narrows tenant scope and does not justify an unrelated architecture rewrite. No new scheduler, hydration cache, outbox or global reconciliation worker was introduced; the nearby webhook purge retains bounded1000-row batches/100-batch cap. BFF/public sends make one explicit adapter send; Typebot's per-response message loop retains approved behavior and is triggered only for the winning accepted IN. MessageAcceptance uses the PostgreSQL resource/externalId unique key, identity fence through commit and BU/contact advisory locking, limiting duplicate Message/unread/realtime/bot effects rather than retrying remote sends.

Provider operations were inspected beyond fake-port call totals: authorize is exchange plus token debug (two HTTP requests); options is one token debug and optionally one explicitly requested phone page; confirm is token debug plus the selected page and optionally one register (maximum three); advance/retry has one subscription operation, and ambiguous register/subscription/code exchange never replays automatically. Meta pages request limit100 and use an explicit cursor limited to512 characters; no remote next URL is followed. Evolution uses the named instanceName filter in one fetchInstances request and checks the exact name. Pairing worst-case create/lookup/QR combinations have at most three requests, while old-instance cleanup uses at most lookup+delete and returns before creating a replacement in a later round. Verify uses at most two Meta reads or one Evolution lookup; disconnect cleanup uses at most lookup+delete. Each adapter fetch has a ten-second AbortSignal timeout and rejects redirects; per-channel CAS leases are45 seconds. HTTP occurs outside DB transactions, and current attempt/generation/epoch/lease/session/grant are rechecked around provider work. These are local budget and fencing properties, not provider exactly-once guarantees.

EPS: required/medium EPS-E2, EPS-SP-STRONG, EPS-A2. Raw cp21-final-all.log:400 plus number-onboarding-pcv.e2e-spec.ts provide an actual JSON EXPLAIN on25 attempts and20 authenticated endpoint read timings: median7.469ms, p95 9.445ms, maximum9.948ms. PostgreSQL chose Seq Scan on the tiny idempotency fixture; the appropriate unique index exists, so this alone is not an indexing regression and does not prove index use at volume. The sample meets the strong-query-evidence portion of EPS-E2 and correctly makes no SLO/capacity claim. However, the access-path audit is incomplete at the newly found resolver locus, so EPS-A2/full lane acceptance must remain withheld until NUM-PERF-01 and its query-path evidence are resolved. The measured GET route is not the exact SQL idempotency lookup, and neither measurement covers the inverse identity relation.

FRC: required/high FRC-E3, FRC-SP-H, FRC-A1. I accept the observed sample and invariants. Actual browser test lines343-434 holds each real BFF reservation response after route.fetch; five waves each inject20 additional submit events after the initial click. Raw log:1199 records100 repeated triggers, reservations[1,1,1,1,1], inFlightAtBarrier[1,1,1,1,1] and maximum1. Product code checks the synchronous operationRef before lifecycle invalidation (CadastroNumero.tsx:269-282), with one operation owner, monotone DTO versions/generations and lifecycle invalidation. A separately held real RESERVED read is released after authoritative cancellation, its requestfinished event is awaited, and the final UI stays cancelled. This is a discriminating stale-result control, not a fake success response or merely a disabled button. In-flight here measures held UI reservation responses, not provider/global concurrency; the simultaneous request counts give the relevant amplification control. Nearby SDK callback/lifecycle cases and operation-owner tests support the rest of the policy. Attempt polling is sequential at five seconds, stops on terminal state/lifecycle and has a60-read per-effect cap; list polling coalesces an existing read, and forced action refreshes are bounded. The historical21-request defect is fixed and is not re-raised.

BCI: required/high BCI-E3, BCI-SP-H, BCI-A1. I accept the observed deterministic overlap sample and local invariants. number-onboarding-bci.e2e-spec.ts and raw log:333 establish five repetitions of20 concurrent same-key creates, followed by20 confirmation operations consisting of one held provider-port winner plus19 duplicates. This is two20-operation phases per repetition, not40 simultaneous operations. All creates return201 with one attempt and one nonce; the database count is one, mismatched payloads409, held duplicates409 and one confirmation crosses the port. Candidate removal and promoted state are checked. Verify/delete overlap, replacement channel identity and retained ownership are read back; the15 fake confirmation calls include the later verification/rebinding controls and are not15 real Graph HTTP requests. The separate raw log:336 sample has five20-operation rounds (one held create, nine busy pairs, ten busy deletes), one provider-port call at each barrier, subsequent delete/recreate with distinct identities, retained cleaned tombstones and an ATENDENTE negative control with zero additional provider calls. The explicit invariant is PAIR-LEASE-GENERATION-IDENTITY; policy is one valid lease winner, busy requests before provider work and cleanup before replacement. These are real PostgreSQL/HTTP boundary tests with external-port doubles; they do not certify actual Meta/Evolution mutation semantics or exactly-once side effects.

RLS: recommended/medium RLS-E1, RLS-SP-L, RLS-A1 with the approved before_local_implemented deadline. I accept the one bounded stage sample. number-onboarding-pcv.e2e-spec.ts:64-104 starts five authenticated clients concurrently; each performs three own-BU and three foreign-tenant reads sequentially, totaling30 checks, with a single owned loopback listener. Raw log:403 records every expected200/404, correct channel projection and zero Meta/Evolution read-stage deltas after a positive Meta counter calibration (before/after Meta1, Evolution0). The counter wraps every relevant adapter-port operation. These statuses and zero external calls are the stated thresholds and are compared by assertions. Elapsed82.065ms is an observation, not a latency threshold, throughput or sustained-pressure measurement. This fulfills the explicitly bounded local RLS profile; CPU/memory/saturation/SLO and real-provider load remain unmeasured, without an implicit waiver or reduced sample.

Evidence limits: cp21 all exited0 with21 migrations, API138 unit/282 PG E2E, Web28 unit and44 browser tests; raw log SHA256 b5466cf71c12cd882e189f8aa1ad333233edea969dfebb46b809f6eff4149725 was verified. The complete214 public snapshot was captured after API E2E and before Web build/browser, then matched after all; it is not a complete pre-all snapshot. The73 changed-input pre-all manifest, read-only binds/public dotenv masks and pre-worker served-bundle attestation complement that limitation. The later start-channels-local.sh WSLENV-only delta matches the final source manifest and has separate syntax/diff/config-only proof; I do not attribute it to the earlier all run. Raw PCV JSON log payloads are credible observations but are not complete pcv-1 final evidence envelopes: actual independent reviewer identities, run/environment/executor linkage, canonical self-hash and lane rows must be supplied during root consolidation. Pending canonical rows must not be claimed passed solely from a green test log.

Elegance is acceptable: one scoped credential resolver, one keyed message acceptance owner, explicit external adapters and one frontend operation owner keep the frozen intent recognizable. The substantial state-machine/check repetition is justified by current required security/lifecycle boundaries; cosmetic extraction is not a delivery blocker. Structural soundness is mixed because the otherwise coherent unique/CAS/tombstone design omits the resolver access index/key. Operational fit is mixed: own local namespace, disposable validation DB, pinned Evolution, gateway/header/log-rotation/HTTPS proofs and WSLENV config proof support the local operator exercise, while actual Meta authorization, device pairing and real IN/OUT remain pending and block overall ST-CON-01 completion. The npm audit remains8 affected entries (1critical/6high/1moderate). Its authenticated Multer DoS is concrete existing debt in BLG-leadshug-runtime-dependency-security; the packet's operator-only cohort limits its current disposition and body-size limits do not cure it. I do not adopt the separate diagnostic as this lane's security judgment or reopen already adjudicated dependency debt without changed exposure. No zero-finding or broad dependency-upgrade criterion is imposed.
recommended_path: Keep local delivery and EPS acceptance conditional on NUM-PERF-01, rather than recording all four PCV lanes passed now. Resolve the exact reverse-identity query with an indexed exact-resource lookup or a versioned FK-side index, preserve durable owners/tenant checks, and obtain query evidence for that actual path. Root should then adjudicate this independent result and derive four machine-checkable pcv-1 evidence artifacts from the verified raw run with explicit EPS-E2/A2, FRC-E3/A1, BCI-E3/A1 and RLS-E1/A1 profile assignments, actual distinct executor/reviewer identities, run/environment/source linkage and canonical SHA256; reflect honest lane states in the governing TODO. I accept the existing FRC-SP-H, BCI-SP-H and bounded RLS-SP-L samples at their stated limits; a repeat of unchanged successful profiles is not needed solely to eliminate debt or relabel old evidence. The EPS measurement exists but needs the material access-path correction above. Preserve the plan's ten-second requests,45-second per-channel leases, bounded manual pages, absence of list-provider fan-out and no remote-mutation replay. Continue the private temporary operator-only integration exercise only under the separately established runtime/security conditions; retain authenticated upload dependency debt before admitting untrusted authenticated users. Actual Meta/device/IN/OUT proof for both modalities, remaining independent lanes and final root dispositions still govern overall close; this review cannot turn local readiness into Production-Ready or authorize push/deployment/callback takeover. STOP after writing only this advisory result; no product, runtime, canonical-document or other artifact edits were made.
